lines: Gustave Eiffel hoisted a large flag atop his new iron tower.
Nothing 300 metres tall had ever been built.
In 1887, famous French artists protested against it.
Their petition called the tower useless and monstrous.
They said it would loom over Paris like a gigantic black smokestack.
And high up, there was the wind.
Eiffel said wind resistance was his primary concern.
His engineers had sketched four lattice girders, open frames of crossing iron.
Eiffel said wind loads had shaped the curve of its four edges.
That rule removed the need for cross-bracing, extra diagonal bars.
Melt down all 7,300 tonnes of iron.
It would cover the base just 6.25 centimetres deep.
You see, it's like a basket: mostly air, yet strong.
The air around it weighs almost as much as the iron.
In the wind, the tower sways by up to 9 centimetres.
The tower's top two-thirds do use cross-bracing.
His wind story made the odd shape seem necessary, not chosen.
It may have been his answer to the artists who called it monstrous.

claims.claim: On 31 March 1889 Eiffel led officials to the top of the tower and hoisted a large Tricolour.
When proposed, nothing equalling the Tower's 300m height had ever been built.
The petition 'Artists against the Eiffel Tower', published on 14 February 1887, protested against this useless and monstrous Eiffel Tower, dominating Paris like a gigantic black smokestack.

Eiffel said the phenomenon he had to give primary concern in designing the Tower was wind resistance; Koechlin's sketch showed four lattice girders standing apart at the base and coming together at the top.

Eiffel declared the curved silhouette was determined by the pattern of wind loads, a principle that removed the need for cross-bracing; however, cross-bracing has been used in the Tower's top two-thirds, and the principle portrayed the profile as a technical necessity rather than an aesthetic choice.

If the 7,300 tonnes of metal were melted down it would fill the square base to a depth of only 6.25 cm; the air in a box around the tower weighs almost as much as the iron; the tower sways by up to 9 cm in the wind.

cast.eiffel: a 56 year old French engineer, upright build, greying swept-back hair, a neatly trimmed full grey-streaked beard, bright alert eyes, a charcoal grey frock coat, a white wing collar and a black silk cravat, 1880s
cast.garnier: a 61 year old French architect, stout build, wild curly white hair, a bushy white beard, a round red face, a black velvet jacket and a wide floppy crimson bow tie, 1880s
cast.koechlin: a 28 year old slim Swiss engineer, neat short light brown hair, a thin light brown moustache, small wire spectacles, white shirt sleeves rolled up and a tan waistcoat, 1880s
